outcome: No proof, disproof, or narrowing of Schanuel's conjecture itself has appeared since 26 January 2024; all post-2024 work found is either an analogue/variant conjecture in a different setting (elliptic/quasi-elliptic functions, 1-motives) or exploratory AI-assisted mapping of the problem's proof landscape with no claimed progress.
summary: Schanuel's conjecture (transcendence degree ≥ n of a field generated by n Q-linearly-independent complex numbers together with their exponentials) remains open, and no development since 26 January 2024 changes what a careful person would write in this bullet. I found three categories of post-2024 material. (1) Genuine analogue/variant conjectures, not cases of the stated problem: Bertolin & Waldschmidt, 'Variations on Schanuel's Conjecture for elliptic and quasi-elliptic functions I: the split case' (arXiv:2504.14048, submitted April 2025), which states and studies a Schanuel-style conjecture for elliptic/quasi-elliptic functions rather than the exponential function on which the original conjecture is stated; and Bertolin, 'A conjecture in Schanuel style for 1-motives' (arXiv:2509.08700, September 2025), which formulates a new conjecture for 1-motives (proving a special case of the Grothendieck-André periods conjecture in that different, motivic setting). Both are explicitly analogues 'in Schanuel style' over different mathematical objects (elliptic curves / 1-motives instead of Gm and Ga), which per §3.1 is a related problem, not a restriction of the stated one — settling them removes no territory from the original conjecture about ordinary complex exponentials. (2) A Princeton colloquium abstract (Nov 2025) describing work of Pila (with Binyamini, Kiro, Kozma) 'between Schanuel's Conjecture and Fuglede's Conjecture' — this is again a distinct, intermediate statement, not a proof of a case of Schanuel's conjecture itself, and I found no preprint establishing that it settles any restriction of Schanuel's own statement. (3) ProofAtlas (proofatlas.ai), described as 'AI-first mathematical research' infrastructure, hosts a page mapping the proof landscape around Schanuel's conjecture (2,630 lines of investigation, a partial conditional reduction, identified open gaps such as a 'delta-domain continuation lemma'). The page explicitly states 'Revision v6 explicitly reports no proof' and characterizes its own output as exploration of routes and obstacles, not a mathematical result — nothing here is a checked or published proof of any part of the conjecture, so it does not count as progress under §3.1, and even if it did, there is no authors'-own-account claim of what an AI system specifically produced mathematically (ai_role therefore none). The Wikipedia article itself, checked live, cites no post-2018 developments. Baker's theorem, Lindemann-Weierstrass, and other proven special cases are all pre-2024 and were already known before the frozen revision, so they are not relevant events for this window. I searched arXiv, Google Scholar-style web search, Terence Tao's public writing, and the ProofAtlas page directly; nothing surfaced a case settled, a bound moved on the conjecture's own statement, or a withdrawn/incident AI claim.
competing_reading: One could argue the elliptic/quasi-elliptic and 1-motive 'Schanuel-style' conjectures are conceptually continuous with the original and that proving the split semi-elliptic case (which the Bertolin-Waldschmidt paper shows implies several Schneider-type theorems) constitutes indirect progress worth noting as `progress`. I judge this the wrong classification because the objects of study (elliptic exponential maps, 1-motives) are different from the ordinary exponential function that Schanuel's conjecture is stated over — these are variants sharing a name and proof philosophy, not restrictions of the same statement, matching the triage's assessment.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement that proves any nontrivial case of the original Schanuel's conjecture (Q-linear independence hypothesis on ordinary complex numbers z_1,...,z_n implying transcendence degree ≥ n for Q(z_1,...,z_n,e^{z_1},...,e^{z_n})), or that meaningfully narrows the conjecture as literally stated — as opposed to an analogue over a different exponential-like map.
